Relevant text: float16 and bfloat16 'are only half the size of float32' and 'reduce the memory required to train a network, allowing for larger models, larger batches, or larger inputs'; torch.amp autocast with float16 or bfloat16; bfloat16's dynamic range equals float32's. Gradient accumulation (summing gradients over several small batches before one optimizer step, so the effective batch is their total) is common practice described in third-party guides seen as search results on 2026-11-17 (to verify against the PyTorch documentation). The out-of-memory message text in the scenario is authored in PyTorch's format.

brief.situation: You are the ML engineer on call for Brightmoor Grocers, a fictional supermarket chain. The demand-forecast model retrains every night as a custom training job on one NVIDIA L4 GPU (24 GB) in us-central1, and the 05:00 forecast run needs the new model. Tonight's job failed two minutes in. Training takes about two and a half hours, so a healthy job must be running by 02:30.
handover: Yesterday PR-381 ('faster nightly retrain') was merged into the training config.
Last night's job succeeded on the same machine type.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the training job, its accelerator and the model registry.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the job failed, what configuration you chose and why, and how you know it will finish in time.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects the out-of-memory error to the config change and the GPU's capacity.
parts.modelAnswer: The job failed at step 0 with CUDA out of memory at batch 256; PR-381 had raised the batch from 64 (peak 9.6 GiB at fp32) to 256, which does not fit the L4's 22 GiB.

parts.label: Choice
parts.criteria: Keeps the tuned effective batch instead of just shrinking it, and rules out hardware that is not available.
parts.modelAnswer: Micro-batches of 64 with four accumulation steps keep the effective batch of 256 the retuned learning rate expects, and bf16 autocast halves activation memory. Reverting the batch alone would mismatch the learning rate; there is no A100 quota tonight.

parts.label: In time
parts.criteria: Checks progress and memory before closing.
parts.modelAnswer: The new job passed step 500 with loss in line with last night and peak memory 16.2 GiB, running before 02:30, so the model will be registered before the 05:00 forecast.

scoring.modelReasoning: The job failed at step 0 with CUDA out of memory, and the only change is PR-381, which raised the batch from 64 to 256 at full fp32 precision and retuned the learning rate for that batch. Last night's run peaked at 9.6 GiB at batch 64, so 256 cannot fit an L4's 22 GiB. Retrying unchanged fails the same way, and the project has no A100 quota tonight. Reverting the batch to 64 would fit but leave the learning rate tuned for 256. Keep the effective batch at 256 with four micro-batches of 64 and gradient accumulation, and use bfloat16 autocast to halve activation memory; then confirm the job is past its first steps with sensible loss and memory before 02:30.
